Export a reproducible communication project

Source: R/communication.R
cata_export.Rd

Writes a new directory containing input and selected-data snapshots, an R script, report and dashboard HTML, Quarto sources, and a local Shiny dashboard. The R script reconstructs selected data using the supplied preparation steps, then recomputes summaries and the chart. It uses an input RDS snapshot to preserve identifiers, factors, dates and column types.

Usage 

cata_export(
  data,
  directory,
  input = data,
  steps = character(),
  join_data = NULL,
  plot_args = NULL,
  summary_spec = NULL,
  chart_data = c("records", "summary"),
  audit = NULL,
  title = "Data analysis report",
  question = "",
  methods = "",
  finding = "",
  limitations = "",
  source = "",
  unit = "",
  denominator = "",
  width = 8,
  height = 5
)

Arguments

data

Selected analysis data.

directory

A new output directory; existing directories are protected.

input

Original input snapshot, before the listed preparation steps.

steps

Character vector of R preparation statements, each operating on analysis.data. These are written to the exported script, not executed by this function. Only export statements you have reviewed.

join_data

Optional reference-table snapshot used by preparation steps.

plot_args

Named arguments for cata_plot(), excluding data.

summary_spec

Optional arguments for cata_count_status(), excluding data. The status summary is recomputed when the project is run.

chart_data

Use selected records or the status summary for the chart.

audit

Optional preparation log.

title, question, methods, finding, limitations, source, unit, denominator

Author-supplied report text.

width, height

Figure dimensions in inches, retained in the project.

Value

The new directory, invisibly. Source files are generated even when Quarto is not installed. HTML exports need neither Quarto nor a server.

Examples 

# \donttest{
out <- tempfile("cata-project-")
cata_export(data.frame(value = 1:5), out, title = "Example report")
# }
